차.x: Have a cup of warm tea.
차.t: 차 also means 'car' (車) — context makes it clear. Tea names: 녹차, 홍차, 보리차.

차.x: My father goes to work by car.
차.t: Homonym: 차 also means tea (茶). Context tells you which: 차를 마셔요 vs 차를 타요.

원피스.ex: 친구 결혼식에 파란 원피스를 입고 갔어요.
원피스.x: I wore a blue dress to my friend's wedding.
원피스.t: Konglish: 원피스 means a woman's dress, not a one-piece swimsuit.

무릎.ex: 어제 등산을 많이 해서 무릎이 아파요.
무릎.x: I hiked a lot yesterday, so my knees hurt.
무릎.e: Also means 'lap': 무릎에 앉다 = to sit on someone's lap.
무릎.t: Alone it sounds like [무릅], but the ㅍ comes back before a vowel: 무릎이 [무르피].

틀리다.m: to be wrong, to get wrong
틀리다.x: I got two questions wrong on the test.
틀리다.t: Many speakers say 틀리다 for 'different', but standard Korean uses 다르다 for that.

삶다.x: Put the eggs in a pot and boil them for 10 minutes.
삶다.e: Think 삶은 계란 'boiled egg'. Don't confuse it with 삶 'life', from 살다.
삶다.t: Use 삶다 for solid food like eggs or noodles; use 끓이다 for water, soup or stew.

씨.ex: 지영 씨, 오늘 점심 같이 먹을래요?
씨.x: Jiyoung, do you want to have lunch together today?
씨.e: Originally 'clan, family name'; now a polite title after a person's name.
씨.t: Use after a given name or full name, never alone with a surname for seniors or with your own name.

익숙하다.m: to be used to, to be familiar with
익숙하다.ex: 처음에는 매웠지만 이제 한국 음식에 익숙해졌어요.
익숙하다.x: It was spicy at first, but now I've gotten used to Korean food.
익숙하다.e: Probably related to 익다 (to ripen; to get used to) — what's 'ripe' is familiar.
익숙하다.t: N에 익숙하다 = be used to N; add -해지다 for 'get used to'. Pronounced [익쑤카다].

소비자.ex: 소비자들은 싸고 품질이 좋은 물건을 원해요.
소비자.x: Consumers want things that are cheap and good quality.
소비자.e: -자 = person who does it: 소비자, 과학자, 운전자.

자신감.x: When my teacher praises me, I gain confidence.

풍습.ex: 설날에 떡국을 먹는 것은 한국의 오래된 풍습이에요.
풍습.x: Eating rice cake soup on Lunar New Year is an old Korean custom.
풍습.e: Literally 'the wind and habits' of a place — its way of life.

외삼촌.x: My maternal uncle is my mother's younger brother.
외삼촌.e: 외 marks the mother's side; 삼촌 means 'three degrees' of kinship.

로맨스.ex: 저는 슬픈 영화보다 로맨스 영화를 좋아해요.
로맨스.x: I like romance movies more than sad movies.
로맨스.t: Combines with other genres, as in 로맨스 판타지; 로맨틱 코미디 is shortened to 로코.

보험료.x: The older you are, the more expensive insurance premiums get.
보험료.t: Pronounced [보험뇨]. 보험료 is what you pay; 보험금 is what you receive.

미술품.ex: 이 박물관에는 귀한 미술품이 많이 있어요.
미술품.x: This museum has many valuable works of art.

만화가.ex: 제 꿈은 유명한 만화가가 되는 거예요.
만화가.x: My dream is to become a famous cartoonist.

공약.ex: 그 후보는 공약을 모두 지키겠다고 말했어요.
공약.x: That candidate said he would keep all his campaign promises.

홀가분하다.x: All my exams are over, so I feel so much lighter.
홀가분하다.t: Also used for traveling light: 짐이 없어서 홀가분해요 (No luggage, so I feel free).

괴로움.ex: 그는 실수 때문에 오랫동안 괴로움에 시달렸어요.
괴로움.x: He was tormented for a long time because of his mistake.
괴로움.e: Noun from 괴롭다 (to be painful); the ㅂ becomes 우.

어이없다.ex: 그렇게 쉬운 문제를 틀리다니 정말 어이없어요.
어이없다.x: I can't believe I got such an easy question wrong. It's ridiculous.
어이없다.e: 어이 + 없다 'to lack'; 어이 alone is not used, so learn it as a unit.
어이없다.t: Pronounced [어이업따]; as a modifier, use 어이없는, not 어이없은.

그만큼.m: that much, to that extent, as much
그만큼.x: The more you exercise, the healthier you get.
그만큼.e: 그 'that' + 만큼 'as much as': literally 'as much as that'.

응답하다.x: Thank you for responding to the survey.
응답하다.t: Used for surveys, calls and requests; 대답하다 is the everyday word for answering a question.

뒤지다.m: to fall behind, to lag; to rummage, to search through
뒤지다.x: I rummaged through my whole bag looking for my keys.
뒤지다.e: Two homonyms: 'lag behind' and 'rummage' — context tells which.
뒤지다.t: Careful: in rude slang 뒤지다 also means 'to die', so watch your context.

간이 크다.forms: 간이 커요 · 간이 컸어요 · 간이 큰 (+noun) (ㅡ drops)
간이 크다.ex: 혼자 밤에 산에 가다니 정말 간이 크네요.
간이 크다.x: Going to the mountain alone at night? You've really got guts.
간이 크다.e: Literally 'to have a big liver'—Koreans locate courage in the liver, not the heart.
간이 크다.t: Can be praise or a scolding for recklessness: 간이 부었다 'you've gotten too bold'.

정주행.m: binge-watching (a series from start to finish)
정주행.ex: 주말 동안 드라마 한 시즌을 정주행했어요.
정주행.x: I binge-watched a whole season of a drama over the weekend.
정주행.e: Literally 'driving in the right direction': watching straight through from episode 1, the opposite of 역주행.
정주행.t: The verb is 정주행하다; also used for reading a whole webtoon from the start.

재분배.ex: 세금은 소득 재분배에 중요한 역할을 합니다.
재분배.x: Taxes play an important role in income redistribution.

기사화.m: being reported as a news story, coverage
기사화.ex: 그 사건은 다음 날 여러 신문에 기사화되었습니다.
기사화.x: The incident was reported in several newspapers the next day.
기사화.e: Literally 'turning into an article'; -화 = -ize, become: 현대화, 국제화.

범죄율.ex: 이 도시는 범죄율이 낮아서 안전한 편이에요.
범죄율.x: This city has a low crime rate, so it's fairly safe.
범죄율.t: The suffix for 'rate' is 율 after a vowel or ㄴ, and 률 after other batchim: 범죄율, 합격률.

치료제.ex: 아직 이 병에 효과적인 치료제가 없어요.
치료제.x: There is still no effective treatment for this disease.
치료제.e: 치료 = treatment, plus -제 = drug or agent: 치료제, 진통제, 항암제.

폭등하다.ex: 집값이 폭등해서 젊은 사람들이 집을 사기 어려워요.
폭등하다.x: Housing prices have skyrocketed, so it's hard for young people to buy homes.

식상하다.ex: 매일 같은 광고를 보니까 이제 식상해요.
식상하다.x: I see the same ad every day, so now I'm sick of it.
식상하다.e: Literally 'hurt by eating' — like being sick of a food eaten too often.

일제히.m: all at once, simultaneously, in unison
일제히.ex: 공연이 끝나자 관객들이 일제히 박수를 쳤어요.
일제히.x: When the show ended, the audience applauded all at once.
일제히.e: Literally 'evened out as one' — everyone at the same moment.

넌지시.ex: 엄마에게 생일 선물에 대해 넌지시 물어봤어요.
넌지시.x: I casually asked my mom about my birthday present, dropping hints.
넌지시.t: Used when you hint at something without saying it outright.

동맹.ex: 한국과 미국은 오랫동안 동맹 관계를 유지해 왔습니다.
동맹.x: Korea and the United States have maintained an alliance for a long time.

부가 가치.ex: 이 제품은 디자인으로 부가 가치를 높였어요.
부가 가치.x: This product increased its added value through design.
부가 가치.t: On Korean receipts, 부가세 is short for 부가 가치세, the VAT.

선제공격.ex: 그 나라는 선제공격의 가능성을 배제하지 않았습니다.
선제공격.x: That country did not rule out the possibility of a preemptive strike.

개화기.ex: 개화기에는 신문과 전차 같은 새로운 문물이 들어왔어요.
개화기.x: During the Enlightenment period, new things like newspapers and streetcars arrived.

일간지.ex: 아버지는 매일 아침 일간지 두 개를 읽으세요.
일간지.x: My father reads two daily newspapers every morning.
일간지.t: 일간지 uses the 지 for 'paper', while 주간지 and 월간지 use a different 지 meaning 'record'.

여미다.ex: 바람이 너무 차서 코트 깃을 여몄어요.
여미다.x: The wind was so cold that I pulled my coat collar together.
여미다.e: Pictures overlapping the front flaps of a hanbok and fastening them neatly.
